scope: Dated journal artwork evidence and original plot-selection methods. Requirements apply only to the recorded journal, artwork type and submission stage. Third-party styles are not official acceptance criteria.

claims.layout: Compact alphabetical panel order where possible; size panels for content legibility

sources.limitations: The guide refers specifically to Nature widths, not every Nature Portfolio title. Its colour palette is an example, not a mandatory branded palette. Text contrast requirement is for text; do not impose it on every pair of data colours. Raster photographs may be embedded in editable vector composites. claims.scale_bars: Use scale bars rather than magnification; keep bars and labels on editable layers
claims.decorative_elements: Avoid gridlines, drop shadows, clutter, overlapping and coloured text

sources.limitations: 300 dpi is for photographic imagery, not a reason to rasterize graphs. Upsampling does not recover missing image detail. Context-specific gridlines may still support interpretation in a general scientific figure; this is Nature house guidance.

claims.legend_statistics: Describe centre values and all error bars/calculations; give n, test and P values

claims.font: Clear sans-serif, e.g. Helvetica, consistent size; numeric pt range not specified on this page

claims.panel_relation: Multiple panels only when logically connected

sources.limitations: Do not copy Nature's 0.25–1 pt range into this profile: Nature Communications explicitly requires the thinnest final line >=1 pt. Page does not provide a numeric standard font size. 1040/2080 pixels are the official rounded examples; at exactly 300 dpi use ceil(mm/25.4*300), i.e. 1040/2126 pixels for 88/180 mm, to satisfy both intended physical width and resolution.

sources.title: Data visualization: A view of every Points of View column
sources.authority: official Nature Methods blog summary and linked primary articles
sources.stage: scientific communication advice, not submission rules

claims.use: Public topic-based index: composition, colour, plot types, multidimensional data and exploration

sources.limitations: Original post dated 2013 and later updated; useful discovery index, not a current numerical journal specification. Several full Points of View papers are subscription-only; only publicly visible summaries/captions were used where noted.

sources.title: Kick the bar chart habit
sources.authority: Nature Methods editorial, full text accessible

claims.guidance: Bars suit counted values. For statistical samples prefer mean-and-error or box plots; a bar of the sample mean hides the underlying distribution. A connected mean-and-error display can emphasize a trend.

sources.limitations: Communication advice, not prohibition of all bars; does not mandate one summary method for every experiment.

sources.title: Visualizing samples with box plots

claims.guidance: Box plots describe sample spread and differences. Public Figure 2 caption advises avoiding them for very small samples (n<5); Figure 3 notes quartiles are more intuitive for skewed samples than mean and SD.

sources.limitations: Current official web page exposes preview and figure captions, not the full article. The n<5 guidance is methodological advice, not a journal acceptance gate. Do not infer reliable population density from small samples.

sources.title: Show the dots in plots
sources.authority: Nature Biomedical Engineering editorial, full text accessible

claims.guidance: Show individual observations when feasible, including overlaid dots if bars are useful. Means and spread can hide distinct distributions and dependent-sample patterns. Dense scatter can become crowded for large samples.

sources.limitations: Editorial recommendation; large-sample crowding is data- and layout-dependent, not a universal n threshold requiring density estimates.

sources.title: Heat maps

claims.guidance: Heat maps can present multivariate data; apply colour, order/clustering and parallel-coordinate alternatives according to the analytical question.

sources.limitations: Preview/figure captions and official index available; full text not inspected. No claim that a heatmap is mandatory for all matrices.

sources.title: Mapping quantitative data to color

claims.guidance: Select colour maps according to data structure; colour is a compact encoding for large datasets.

sources.limitations: Public abstract and official index were inspected; article full text/PDF unavailable through current fetch. Sequential versus diverging map choice below is explicitly a practice synthesis, not quoted mandatory policy.

sources.title: Temporal data

claims.guidance: Use time's inherent properties when choosing the visual representation.

sources.limitations: Only public preview/figure description inspected. XY line/marker recommendation below is a reasoned application, not a journal rule.

sources.title: Unentangling complex plots

claims.guidance: Carefully designed subplots can communicate better than a complicated single overview; public figure caption describes small multiples and progressive cropping for traces at different y ranges.

sources.limitations: Public preview/figure captions only. Use consistent scales when visual cross-panel comparisons require them, and disclose different scales; shared limits are not universally mandated by this paper.

sources.title: Into the third dimension

claims.guidance: 3D visualization is useful for real spatial data and rarely for other data types.

sources.limitations: Public preview inspected. This discourages decorative 3D; it does not forbid legitimate spatial/surface representations.

sources.title: Association, correlation and causation
sources.limitations: Public preview inspected; scatterplot selection below is an analytical practice synthesis. A fitted line requires its own model and uncertainty checks.
